text: You sink your teeth into that first slice of square pizza pie from meta pizza-slinger Square Pie and triumphant victory is yours from the very first bite. Couldn't decide between red sauce options of pepperoni cups or glistening, crumbly sausage morsels, so the solution to that problem was...spinach. Spinach wound up being most royally bomb. It was the right choice. The creamy mellowness of milky ricotta clouds dolloped with wild abandon (but not too recklessly) is positively dreamy, especially paired with the nutty saltiness of grana padano cheese, along with piles of tender, garlicky spinach. Drizzles of luscious herb oil create a blissful cohesion, pooling into tiny puddles and adding another sensational level of savory depth. And the garlic. This pie is beautifully ample on the garlic front, damn. If you can muster the restraint to save a couple of slices for later, do it. And then eat them after they've cooled down for awhile. My pizza gauge takes into account how good a slice is when eaten cold. It can't not. How does the slice taste at 5am the next day, or whenever desperation kicks in later? This is important. Then there's that ridiculous romaine salad on the menu, which includes fresh chopped romaine, a hard boiled egg, roasted tomatoes, artichokes, about a quarter pound of shredded sharp provolone, and a piquant red wine vinaigrette. It's unmistakably savory all the way through; delightfully briny and tangy and delicious, with satisfyingly on-point ratios. Rip open a piece of crust and shove some in it. The end.

text: Bourbon Street and all of it's fame is a half block away, but this deserves to be one of the most famous spots in the French Quarter. Before we get to anything else - they are serious about that dress code and they seem to always be packed. Do yourself a favor and plan ahead if you want to visit. The menu changes often, so it's possible to miss out on the dish you wanted if you have to come back the next day. There are some inventive dishes here - the Tempura Fin wings somehow get all of the great parts of chicken wings but are made from fish. They used to call canned tuna the "chicken of the sea" but this is something different and delicious - they turn the fin section of the catch of the day into a great snack - they take the part that you normally throw away and make it great. I know it's a seafood restaurant, but the pork chop is worth it - the sides and preparation changes often, but it is excellent. The star of the menu is the scalibut - part scallop, part halibut and all good. The scallops are thinly sliced and use as a crust for the halibut, sealing in the flavors and providing a different texture than you would expect. It may sound strange, but it's great. This is an expensive dinner - there were people there celebrating birthdays and other special occasions, so I would suggest making one up to give yourself an excuse to go there and eat. A solid five star place.

text: I write this poor review as a food service professional, though not as a competitor. I'm deeply concerned about how little most establishments contribute to their communities because they don't understand or practice basic synergistic principles. I get that Cat Cora started this chain, and that she was on Iron Chef--but how does that translate into quality and value? The short answer is it doesn't. Gimmick food isn't in itself valuable. Extracting value from employees or customers by producing as little as possible for as much as possible doesn't create value for anyone. That approach is a dead end street. Today's foray into the Goleta shop didn't result in a purchase--for reasons I will lay out shortly. However, I have eaten a Mesa Burger at the Mesa location--it was so-so. I can get an equivalent burger or better at the original Habit in Goleta (yup, smaller patty, but better overall flavor, price and experience). No, today's experience resulted in us walking out before we had even made a purchase. And let me tell you why... Any kind of food service (really, any sort of service) business is far more than a production line of food. It is far more than whether that food is quality or not. It is far more than how much profit the operator can achieve. In its potential form, it is an access point to quality in various forms that goes from the operator to the community and back. Here was our experience today: We walked up to the counter with only one small group of about three adults in front of us ordering. There was one young male taking their order and two young females standing by doing nothing, while looking generally in the our direction--new customers. We stood there for some time with the two females alternately talking to each other and staring off into space. One of those females wandered over to the service counter, where she touched her own hair, jean jacket and ear and then laid her head on her arms on the service counter, with her hair on the counter. She then moved back to the main counter (again, facing us) when the other female moved to take a bottle of apple juice out of the cooler and place it on the counter. She then opened the bottle of juice, poured it into a plastic cup and with the same hands she had touched herself with without gloves she grabbed a lid for the cup and affixed it to the cup. None of the three counter employees acknowledged my wife or me during this whole time. Still waiting, my wife and I then conferred with each other standing just behind and to the side of the people ordering--in plain sight of all three employees--and eventually decided we wouldn't participate in this kind of customer service nightmare and walked out (there was no one behind us and maybe 10 customers total in the restaurant; there were clearly at least three cooks in the kitchen; it wasn't in any sense a stressed environment). So, reader, whom are we taking to task? It's not the employees. Their behavior was far from exemplary, but this is about management. (Hint: it's always about management.) If your idea is about making some gimmicky food and then turning it over to a general manager or shift manager and you think you are going to make money or even (as much as I think this isn't in your head or heart at all) be a part of the community and care about the value you create--you are completely blind. This isn't creativity or artistry or even good food. It's crap. You don't do your employees or customers or community any good. Why should any of us shovel money at you for this?

She said she thought they were not gluten free, but it would be better customer service if she took the time to go back to the kitchen to verify and gave a confident answer. Overall I do love this place and I want to be successful, so maybe a few changes to customer service and this place will be five stars!

text: My advice to anyone reading this...West Chester Veterinary Medical Clinic is NOT the place you want to bring your pet. We started bringing our puppy here 4 months ago. The first two visits were great and then it went downhill from there. We've been back numerous times, spending hundreds of dollars each time. They try and tack on tests that are very expensive and not necessary. They seem to like giving you the worst case scenario saying, "It could be this. We can test for it." We've seen 4 different doctors. They don't seem to always be in agreement on things. For example, one said our puppy was underweight and small for her age when the others all said she was perfect. (She's a mutt. How does anyone know how big she's going to get?) The wait can be long to the point where we call from the parking lot, they say they are going to come out to get the dog, and then they don't come out. We even left once because we waited for 45 minutes with no update on when they would be out to get her. I called yesterday due to an illness and was told the vet who saw my dog last would call me back. No response for 29 hours. When the vet called she said she wasn't even in yesterday. So why have her be the vet to call me back? My dog is sick and needs attention! The vet told me to bring the dog right over and she'd take her right away. We ended up sitting in the parking lot for 20 minutes until someone came out to get the dog. Then the waiting for the vet to call with her theories. The dog came back to the car and we waited for a test result. Got a call with the results and was told the technician would be right out with the dog's meds. We waited again...waiting, waiting, waiting. We finally left 1.75 hours after we got there. Technicians...some are great while others are horrible. One time one walked my dog out to the car by pulling her across the parking lot on her leash - literally dragging her. I called and complained to the manager about some things; she was very nice and said she was going to follow up with me the next week. It's been 4 weeks and no call back. Do yourself a favor and go somewhere else. I wish I had. One additional comment: When you call to make an appointment for an illness you hope they can see your pet the same day, right? Well, they always say they don't have any regular appointments available so we'd have to be an "emergency appointment". That means you pay a heck of a lot more for the appointment. $145 (emergency visit) vs $65 (regular appointment).

text: 3.5 I actually stumbled up on this dog park by accident. We have enjoyed bringing our dog to the nearby park before and this time I was riding solo. My boyfriend usually drives so of course I took the wrong turn. However, when I saw a sign for a dog park, I thought it was a great mistake. We parked in the parking lot by the recreation center and saw a sign for the dog park. Perfect! We went down the path, through a tunnel, and then walked out to a big open area in the park. I was a bit confused where the dog park was. I saw another sign that had arrows pointing to the small dog park and the large dog park. It was probably half a mile to the actual dog park. I have a pug so the walk to and from the dog park is already pushing it for her. Plus, the small dog park is hidden back in the corner. I wasn't sure if we were going the right way. We eventually got to the park and I was happy with it. It's not huge, but small dogs don't really need a lot of room. I really appreciate any dog park that has separate areas for small and large dogs. We have stopped going to our usual dog park because the larger dogs continuously harass my little pug (which is understandable because she is so cute). The grass was well kept and clean. I didn't see a single piece of dog poop which is a miracle for a dog park. Our usual park is covered in poop, I mean just covered. Pick up after your dog people! There was a nice bench if you need to sit down while your dog roams about. There was also a drinking fountain for dogs and free poop bags. There were about 5 other dogs at the park but no one bothered my dog. She is really anti-social so this worked well, even though I love other dogs. She walked around and explored for a bit, but then gave me the "Ok time to go home" look. She was pretty tired on the walk back to the car but I guess it's good exercise for her. In the end, the dog park itself is nice. Very clean. The park is a little hard to find and the walk from the parking lot is a bit long if you have a lazy dog like mine. Or like other people have mentioned, if you have an excited dog the anticipation can be a bit much.

My daughter had a very bad accident and lost her front tooth. We were released by the hospital at 8pm after they placed the tooth back into the tooth socket. They explained the tooth most likely would fall out during the night. On our way out of hospital I said let me see if Dr. Metz has an emergency line to call for advice on securing tooth till we could get in to see him. I left a message and within 10 minutes my phone was ringing with Dr. Metz on the line. He took the time to hear the case and asked if I could meet him at office in 15 minutes to assess the tooth and secure the tooth if possible with braces. I was so appreciative he would drive out so late at night to help my daughter. This truly was over and beyond for a Doctor to accommodate us at 9pm on a Saturday. Dr. Metz was amazing and was able to immediately determine the corrective action plan needed for the teeth which was critical to be done to prevent further damage that was caused from the injury to surrounding teeth. Had he not come and fixed with securing teeth with braces we would have had major issues the next day. Dr. Metz immediately reached out to my daughters dentist that night to advise on the injury and coordinated the care plan for her. I am truly speechless and blessed to have found such a wonderful doctor. As a parent there is nothing worse to see your child hurt and not have control. Dr. Metz alleviated so much stress from this horrible accident. Dr. Metz puts his patients first and truly cares. His expertise in complex cases is outstanding and you will be in great hands!! Thank you Dr. Metz!!

All of these statements were incorrect because (1) airport to hotel transfer should have been planned, and scheduled with a driver identified (2) My transfer document from Gate 1 clearly states the airport, arrival flight number of time (3) the local office never offered a car, but rather asked me to take a taxi cab on my own. text: They might have been having an off night, but based on other recent reviews, it just seems this place is suffering from poor management. Had a reservation on Wednesday night for 2 at 7pm that I had made a few days in advance. Was called day of to confirm my reservation. Get there at 6:55 and was asked to wait until our table was ready - no problem. So we wait. And wait. Around 7:20 I go back up to ask how much longer it was going to be and was assured I was next on the list and it would only be 5-10 minutes more. I was a bit peeved as I've never had to wait this long with reservations anywhere, and it wasn't even a busy night, but I had already stuck it out this long. In retrospect, should have just went somewhere else on the loop then and there. We were finally seated around 7:30 and then had to play the waiting game for our waiter, who took about another 10 minutes to appear. She was nice enough, and did apologize for the wait. Having had ample time to review the menu, we promptly placed our order. My drink and our cheese came out fine, salads as well, and having dined here many times in the past I know this part is the experience and it's best to take your time, so no complaints here. It did take some time between salads and the main course. The cooking broth was going for so long before the entrée came out that I was concerned it would all evaporate before we could start cooking. Finally our waiter showed up with the food, again nice but seeming a little out of sorts and apologizing again for our wait. As she was setting down plates I noticed I had a double order of chicken, my boyfriend has a double portion of sirloin, and we were both missing our shrimp, as well as the plum sauce. She apologized, saying she knew it wasn't right but wanted to get something out as we had been waiting for a while, and said she would get our missing items, which she did. Once we were done with dinner it was past 9 pm and I was itching to get out of that place. Even though we ordered a 4-course deal, at that point I couldn't care less about the chocolate, I really didn't want to be there until 10. When she finally returned I let her know, and to my surprise she said we would get a credit for the chocolate portion to use at another time, which was nice. All in all, food was good as always, staff seemed friendly enough, but they definitely struggled with time management. Maybe someone called off, maybe there were issues in the kitchen, I'm not sure, but our waiter seemed frazzled and constantly apologized for the wait, which we sure did plenty off. How is this even an item that an individual has the inclination to pull with all their might and break. After finding the release cable I manually tug on it to open the hood. Set wires in bundles and precariously place it above the brake and clutch pedal. This is disgusting. This was a terrible breach of trust and contract as it was supposed to be a "professional" install done by someone with the acuity greater than that of a 3rd greater. However, don't judge them too harshly on this because there are a lot of good things about this place. For one, you can always find your server, and they serve a high quality of meat compared to most places. Also I really have to say that the red enchilada sauce was unexpectedly spectacular. THIS IS NOT GOOD ENOUGH, particularly when it was clear small children were nearby. In addition to their blatant incompetence and clear disregard for safety, Mr. Knox was incredibly rude when I dared to suggest he had been negligent in not alerting the building department or writing the hazard on the receipt. Let me finish" in response to his repeated interruptions. The scallop hand roll was easily my favorite bite of the night. It was stuffed with fresh scallops which tasted so good with the roe and seaweed. I wish we'd gotten our hand rolls earlier so I still had space to try more, but this one is a MUST! All the rolls were good! For a simpler one (usually my preference) I highly recommend the rainbow roll (not pictured). From the specialty rolls, try the Mr. Pink and Mr. White (this one had a surprising lemony/ herby taste - very refreshing). Of course the green tea mochi and green tea ice cream were a perfect way to end the meal. Can't wait to come back for alllll the hand rolls

Months ago I checked to make sure there were no green bells in either (was assured at the time they are not even part of the recipes). Today, they had a new chef who decided the salad needed them. Of course , when I ordered, I didn't ask (but I had been having this dish for months with no issue so I really didn't see any reason to ask). We discovered the peppers as I was eating the salad. Of course, Miguel's tried to do the right thing (they comped the salad and I did tell them it wasn't necessary). The rest of the meal was fine (in a "well Mrs Lincoln, other than the incident how was the play" kind of thing). That said, it will be a while before I return and I will probably never order the salad. Mostly, this post is two fold. First, for aspiring chefs, when you add ingredients to an established recipe there can be serious consequences (says the guy who is posting this between vomit sessions), so please consider that. There is a lot of construction around the entrance and exit to the airport, so do not follow your GPS. I had a couple of ride-share mishaps that took us to this very scary looking abandoned field instead of the airport, just follow the signage off the highway and navigate the labyrinth of cones. Drop-off here is much easier than pick-up. It is literally the same stretch of road, just at opposite ends of the airport. It is honestly easier to get picked up at the drop-off entrance as the designated pick-up section is small and it gets congested due to the bottle-neck of cars trying to pull out while others are pulling in. I think once the construction mess is done, this airport will reach its full potential, until then 2-stars because they definitely could have better signage navigating to the airport as well as exiting. This is now our new favorite salsa with the right amount of flavor and roasted taste (no it's not spicy but we weren't looking for that). My husband and I loved it so much that we bought 2 extra salsa orders to go. We didn't realize it came in a regular take out container vs. a jar for travel. We ended up purchasing a tightly sealed container from Amazon and now have an extra jar in the freezer for future enjoyment! - Assortment of tacos (pork and carne) - Not the best tacos we've had but it was very delicious, nonetheless. There were some interesting flavors happening that you wouldn't find in most street tacos - Mahi mahi fish platter - WOW! This was by far one of my fave dishes in New Orleans. Super interesting flavors and definitely a "must try" if they have it on the menu. - Mexican corn - I usually love this stuff but their version is a little too sweet for me. - Special shoutout - Their private label hot sauce is the perfect amount of heat and flavor. We also bought 2 bottles of this stuff to take home. Can't wait to return to this city and restaurant once the pandemic is over. What a solid find!
label: POS

text: Since I live around the corner, I have been to Bar Hygge A number of times. Every time has been a positive experience. The ambience is classy, yet not pretentious, and cozy. The prices are a little high, but not outrageous, and the quality of drinks and food is always high. Most recently I went to Bar Hygge on a date. We each got the seasonal punch. We didn't love the first sip, but clearly it grew on us because he got four and I got three. I have had a different seasonal punch in the past, and it was also delicious. This is probably the best bang for your buck drink at Bar Hygge. Since we were there in the evening, we also decided to get one of their boards. We went for the five option board and got the Open Faced Reuben, Fig & Pistachio Terrine, Crispy Brussels, Middle Eastern Caprese, and the Spaghetti Squash Salad. This also came with some bread and a blueberry rosemary butter. Everything was good, but the standouts were the reuben and the terrine. I always want to get Reubens, but they usually come with Swiss cheese (emmental, not gruyere) and mustard, which I hate. However I was excited to see that this Reuben had gruyere, and no mustard! It was everything I always want a Reuben to be, just a lot smaller. The squash on the terrine also added a nice touch. My least favorite item was the Brussel sprouts because I thought they were overly fried and didn't have much flavor. Still, they were decent. Overall, I would give Bar Hygge a 4.5. The food is always good (4/5 stars), but not always as outstanding as the descriptions would make you think. However, since the drinks are creative and delicious, there atmosphere ideal, and since the food is consistently good for how much they change things up, I'll round my 4.5 up to a 5.

text: Sometimes I get on Yelp, sift through the top-rated businesses in STL, and find a place I treasure but have never rated. A place--in this case--I have visited more times than I can count and more times than I would like to admit. But here I am, in my third year of Yelp Elitism and St. Louis residency, never having reviewed Ted Drewes, which is frankly blasphemous and something I must address immediately. Here goes. I live dangerously close to Ted Drewes. Like, I could get a custard craving at 10:45 on a Sunday night, be in line by 10:50, and have my Crater Copernicus with tart cherries by 10:55, five minutes before closing. (This scenario is entirely hypothetical.) For those unfamiliar with frozen custard, it is the richest, smoothest, silkiest variant of ice cream imaginable. My aforementioned favorite is devil's food cake with hot fudge, almonds, and TD's signature vanilla custard, and I add tart cherries. It is legitimately one of the most delicious things I've eaten in my life. If you know someone who doesn't love this place, it's because they didn't visit enough times to find "their thing." Seriously, there are so many options and they're all so good, and you will absolutely find something on the menu that you will fantasize about forever. The hype is real. Ted Drewes is my muse.

text: This place reminds me of every place my parents took us when we were young - that's the early 60s for those of you keeping count... That means there's some good, and some not so good here. Sandwiches were very good, the fries were excellent - greasy and well-fried... Perfect! The ambiance is good, too. Kind of dark - I imagine it will be even darker when we hit the middle of summer -- but feels homey. Lots of tables, we counted 16 five tops in the dining room with a dozen or so booths around the floor as well. Mainly old guys like me in there at lunch. My wife and one other woman being the only reps for the fairer sex in the house. Pretty good menu, and special lunch pricing. Children's menu, too. Now, the "needs work" part. The place has a dingy feel to it. Lots of mirrors on the wall that look like they need a good scrubbing. The tables were clean, and the seats in the booths were clean, but overall, the darkness really added to a feeling that the place needed a good pressure washing. Of course, this all perception, so don't let me put you off think ing the place is grimey... Overall, we'd definitely go back. I'd like to sit at the bar and see how the view is from there. Looks like a good selection and it would be nice to find out if they actually have any of that old-timey beer they had neon signs for... TIP: When you step in the front door, turn around and look up.
